Kitchen Remodeling in Haysville, KS

Haysville is south Sedgwick County's established working-class community, and its housing tells that story plainly. The 1960s through 1980s homes that dominate Haysville's residential areas have kitchens that were functional when they were built and have been wearing out ever since. These aren't homes with trendy builder-grade kitchens from the 2000s — they're older, more honestly built, and more honestly in need of real work.

A 1970s Haysville kitchen typically has original or early-replacement cabinets, a countertop that's been replaced once or maybe twice, a single-basin sink, and a layout that separates the kitchen from the rest of the home. It works. It's just not where anyone wants to spend time. And when the cabinets start to feel loose, the drawer slides are failing, and the countertop is peeling at the backsplash seam for the third time, the calculation changes: fix it again or do it right.

Wheatland Construction does the right version. We're a Veterans Approved Builder (ID: 00899), Home Advisor Certified since 2019, and family-owned since 2018. We've worked in south Sedgwick County's older housing stock and we don't oversell what it needs.

What Haysville Kitchens Typically Need

Older 1960s–1980s homes: The core issue is materials at end of life and layouts that don't serve modern household use. The fix is a real remodel — cabinet replacement, countertop replacement, layout reconfiguration if practical, updated plumbing fixtures, new lighting. We assess structural conditions for any wall removal before quoting.

Cabinet replacement vs. refacing: Haysville's older cabinets split roughly evenly between solid-wood face-frame construction (worth assessing for refacing) and earlier builds with less durable construction (replacement is the better call). We look at box condition and give you an honest recommendation.

Open-concept feasibility: Many Haysville ranch homes have kitchen-dining separation walls that could be opened up. We assess whether it's structural before it becomes a scope item. Not every wall is removable at a reasonable cost — we tell you that too.

Plumbing and electrical: Haysville's older homes sometimes have galvanized pipe at sink connections or older wiring that's worth updating while the kitchen is opened up. We flag these during assessment.

Permits in Haysville

City of Haysville Building Department. We handle all permit applications, fees, and inspection scheduling.

How We Approach Kitchen Remodeling in Haysville

Every kitchen remodel starts with a site visit. We measure the existing layout, look at the plumbing rough-in and drain stack location, check the electrical panel for capacity, and assess structural walls before discussing what's possible. We price in writing with every line item documented.

Our crew handles demo through final walkthrough. Cabinet delivery, tile setting, countertop templating, plumbing trim-out, electrical, and final inspection all coordinated through us - no handoffs to subcontractors who don't know the project.

Wheatland Construction has held Veterans Approved Builder status (ID: 00899) since we opened and has been Home Advisor Certified since 2019. We're licensed and insured in Kansas.

In Haysville, the I-35 south corridor location makes for strong renovation ROI on mid-century and 1980s-90s residential stock. The 1970s-1990s housing stock is aging into full renovation range simultaneously — which means Haysville is currently one of the most active renovation markets in south Sedgwick County. Frequently Asked Questions About Kitchen Remodeling in Haysville

How much does kitchen remodeling cost in Haysville, KS?

Haysville kitchen remodels range from $16,000 for a targeted mid-range refresh to $58,000+ for a full gut renovation with structural changes. These are older working-class homes and we scope and price accordingly — no premium Eastborough pricing applied to a Haysville project. Written, line-item estimates.

Do I need permits for kitchen remodeling in Haysville?

Yes — plumbing, electrical, and structural work requires City of Haysville permits. We handle all permitting.

My 1970s Haysville kitchen cabinets are loose and some drawers have failed — should I replace them?

Probably replace. When the box joints are failing and the drawer slides are wearing out, refacing adds new faces to a failing structure. If the carcasses were solid-wood construction (common in that era), we assess whether they're worth keeping. We'll give you our honest read at the consultation.

Can you open up my Haysville kitchen to the dining area?

We assess structural status first. Some Haysville ranch homes have this wall as a load-bearing or partial-bearing condition that makes the removal expensive. Others are non-structural and the opening is straightforward. We won't quote an open-concept conversion without checking first.

Are there plumbing or electrical concerns in older Haysville homes during a kitchen remodel?

Sometimes. Galvanized pipes at sink connections and original 2-wire electrical are possibilities in homes from the 1960s–1970s. We flag these during assessment and include them in scope when they need to be addressed. It's better to deal with them during the remodel than after the walls are closed.

How long does a Haysville kitchen renovation take?

6–10 weeks from permit issuance. Projects with structural changes or plumbing/electrical updates take toward the longer end.
